notes_blind_original: This case is disputed. The authors' response (https://osf.io/download/698cea243fa4fc8652e24ac1/, Dec 2025) says everything reproduces when chunks are run in the console following the README. They say the stan_lmer error comes from rstanarm 2.32's stricter ellipsis handling. My static check contradicts that explanation. At pinned commit 32cfd57, knitr::purl + parse() of the FINAL Rmd fails with 'unexpected symbol' at em_expert_simple, because 'prior = cauchy(0,c(0.707,0.707,0.5),' is never closed. That is a syntax fault independent of package versions. The README links the Rmd at commit 8db528c, and that version has the identical parse failure. 'Wave 1+2 Analyses update.Rmd' fails parse on 'dplyr::dplyr::select'. Mitigating facts for the reconciler: the Table 1 lay-vs-scientist contrasts (lmer + emmeans revpairwise ~isExpert.factor|domain, Rmd lines ~1182-1187) come before the faulty stan_lmer call in the same chunk and read dat_for_analyses.csv. So line-by-line interactive execution could plausibly produce them, and the dat_long V1/V2 ambiguity does not bear directly on Table 1. The two unreproduced files (contrast1.csv/contrast2.csv) are supplement method contrasts, not Table 1. Nobody has produced Table 1 values from the shipped code. The report did attempt the computation and failed, so the dispute is about who is at fault, not about whether computation was checked. 'Technical failure' is therefore kept with no alternative. Confidence is medium because of the author dispute and the possibility of interactive execution.
